training.disjoint_test_split: test (20 clients per test_sub_list.txt) — untouched by training
training.feature: uniform LBP(8,1) histogram over 80x80 grayscale face crop
training.preprocessing: PittPatt bbox padded 15% on each side before cv2.resize((80,80)) + cv2.cvtColor(BGR2GRAY). Matches Android `FaceCropExtractor.BBOX_PADDING_FRAC=0.15f` — alignment is load-bearing; a drift collapses live-user LBP scores (observed 0.011 on a real face before this fix). The v0.1.0 model was trained without this pad and silently mismatched the mobile pipeline.
training.pickle_to_tflite_parity: max abs delta 5.6e-9 across inner holdout

msu_mfsd_test.protocol: ISO/IEC 30107-3 — APCER and BPCER computed at equal-error threshold on the held-out MSU-MFSD test split
msu_mfsd_test.source: benchmark/ harness, Phase 5 run (v0.2.0 retrain with 15% pad)
msu_mfsd_test.note: AUC regressed marginally from 0.780 (v0.1.0) to 0.767. The pad does not improve MSU in-corpus discrimination — it aligns training preprocessing with the Android inference pipeline, which is what the live-user score collapse required. The optimal threshold of 0.358 well below 0.5 indicates the model is systematically low-scoring; the orchestrator weights (v0.2.0) de-emphasise the LBP branch accordingly and zero out the Fourier branch (pure-math screen-replay detector mis-fires on modern phone captures).

inner_holdout.note: Inner holdout of the MSU-MFSD TRAIN split only — used during training for calibration. NOT a generalization number; use msu_mfsd_test above for that. Live recall 0.518 means roughly half the live samples at the 0.5 threshold get called spoof, which is why layer4_lbp lands around 0.1-0.3 on modern-phone captures — matches the on-device regression that motivated the v0.2.0 orchestrator reweight.

limitations: Trained on MSU-MFSD only — a single corpus of 35 clients captured on 2015-era devices (640×480 Nexus 5 front camera, MacBook Air built-in). Expect degraded performance on modern high-DPI displays, OLED phones, and demographics underrepresented in MSU-MFSD.

Layer 4 LBP is weak on modern phone captures — v0.2.0 reduced its orchestrator weight accordingly and zeroed out the Fourier (screen-replay) branch whose hand-tuned ring-ratio constants also mis-fire on high-resolution modern cameras.

Layer 4 is one of five defense layers. Do not interpret this model's score in isolation — the SDK orchestrator combines it with Layers 2 (challenge), 3 (rPPG), and 5 (behavioral) before emitting liveness_decision.
HTER 0.293 on MSU-MFSD test is a research-grade number, not a production SLA. Treat the SDK's liveness_decision as a strong signal, not a sole authenticator.
